Criteria: Remove or disable access promptly after separation under Meridian’s proposed effective-separation criterion.
Observation: 14 active former-staff accounts found in the six-month review; population denominator unknown.
Impact: Former employees could retain access to business systems.

Criteria: Restrict and review authorized remote access; remove access when authorization ends.
Observation: Three of the 14 active former-staff accounts retained VPN access. Session history was not supplied.
Impact: Former staff could reach internal services remotely.

Criteria: Identify and correct flaws within approved risk-based timelines and verify fixes.
Observation: Six critical and 22 high findings were reported. Oldest critical finding on the shipping file server has been open 90 days.
Impact: A flaw on the server could affect shipping-record confidentiality and availability.

Criteria: Scan on a defined cadence and track findings, ownership and disposition.
Observation: The first scan identifies exposures. No regular review and remediation cadence is evidenced.
Impact: High-risk findings could age without an accountable response.

Criteria: Assess suppliers and review scoped assurance evidence on a defined cadence.
Observation: ShipDesk is business-critical and has never been assessed. SOC 2 evidence has not been provided.
Impact: Meridian lacks assurance over safeguards for delivery records.

Criteria: Define and monitor security requirements for external services.
Observation: Auto-renewing ShipDesk agreement has no security clause.
Impact: Security obligations and remedies are unclear at renewal.

Criteria: Restrict supplier privileges to the minimum scope and duration required.
Observation: ShipDesk support accounts can access Meridian data at any time.
Impact: Unnecessary standing privileges increase exposure to unauthorized access.
